transcript.text:
A fridge-freezer that isn't cold can be caused by simple issues like the temperature setting being turned down too low or food blocking the air vents inside. It could also indicate a fault with the cooling system itself, such as a blocked defrost drain causing ice to build up and stop cold air circulating. To help narrow this down, please check: Is the freezer section still cold (below -18°C) or is it also warming up? Also, can you hear a faint humming from the compressor at the back, and do you hear any fan noise inside?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
freezer still freezing, about -17. motor running loads, and sometimes a faint scraping/ticking from the freezer
AI service unavailable. Please try again in a moment.
hello? got an error. no burning smell or tripping btw. any ideas?

The fact that your freezer is still cold (-17°C) while the fridge isn't suggests the compressor is working fine, but the cold air isn't reaching the fridge compartment. The 'scraping' or 'ticking' noise you hear from inside the freezer often points to an evaporator fan blade hitting a block of ice, which means the defrost system may have failed and ice has built up behind the panels. The most reliable way to check this is to unplug the appliance for 24 hours with both doors open (use towels to catch any meltwater). Once it's fully thawed, plug it back in. If the fridge starts cooling normally again, you have a defrost fault that will likely need an engineer to fix the heater or thermostat.
ok i can do that, have somewhere for the food. will try it and report back

That sounds like a sensible plan. Please go ahead with the full 24-hour defrost as discussed. Once you plug it back in, give it a few hours to cool down properly before checking if the fridge section has returned to normal temperatures. Let me know how it goes.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
did the full defrost. fridge got cold again within a day, was 3C. but after about 5 days it's starting to creep back up again

Since the fridge cooled down after the manual defrost but the problem returned within a few days, this suggests an automatic defect in the cooling system rather than just a blockage. The cold air is being choked off by ice building up again because the appliance isn't melting it away automatically. To find out exactly which part to replace (usually the defrost heater or thermostat), I need the make and model number. sticker inside only says it starts RB34, rest is rubbed off. Samsung. that any use?

That is useful. The 'RB34' prefix identifies it as a Samsung fridge-freezer series. Since the fridge cooled down after your manual defrost but the problem returned within five days, this suggests an automatic defect in the cooling system rather than just a blockage. The cold air is being choked off by ice building up again because the appliance isn't melting it away automatically. The most likely cause is a failed part in the defrost system (usually the heater or thermostat), which prevents the freezer from shedding its internal frost, eventually blocking airflow to the fridge. To distinguish this from a simple blocked drain, please check the bottom of the fridge section (behind the vegetable drawer if there is one) for a small drain hole. Is it clear and dry, or is there water pooling/ice blocking it?
not sure where that is, can't see a drain hole. no veg drawer on mine. didn't see any water pooling though

Since the fridge cooled down after your manual defrost but the temperature crept back up within five days, this suggests a failure in the automatic defrost system. The specific part that has likely failed is either the defrost heater or the defrost thermostat (thermal fuse). Because your Samsung RB34 series appliance is typically covered by a manufacturer warranty, I recommend contacting Samsung directly for a repair. They can send an engineer to replace the faulty component safely and correctly.
